blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
A British business email has a rhythm. It starts with a friendly opening, but not too personal. People write "Hope you're well" or "Hope you had a good weekend."

Then comes the real purpose. The request is often soft. People write "I was wondering if…" or "Would it be possible to…?" This makes the email sound polite.

At the end, you find phrases like "Many thanks", "Best wishes", or the most British of all, "Kind regards." A direct request is not rude. But when you wrap it in polite words, it always lands better.

items.q: How does a British business email usually start?
items.why: "It starts with a friendly opening." O e-mail britânico começa com algo amistoso.

items.q: Which phrase is "the most British of all"?
items.why: "the most British of all, 'Kind regards.'"

items.q: According to the text, a direct request is…
items.why: "A direct request is not rude." Ele só fica melhor quando é suavizado.

items.q: The writer would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: You should be cold and very personal at the same time.
A direct email can still be polite.
"Kind regards" is a good way to close.
Soft words make a request sound polite.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que o tom é amistoso mas NÃO muito pessoal, e nunca frio — a opção mistura ideias que o texto rejeita.

items.q: The phrase "it always lands better" suggests that polite words…
options: help the message be well received
items.why: Inferência: "land better" = ser bem recebido. As palavras educadas ajudam o pedido a ter boa reação.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily falar sobre o e-mail de um colega novo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, come and sit down. I read your email to the client. The English is correct, and thank you for that. But I want to change the tone a little. It sounds too direct for a British client.

Look at the first line. You wrote, "I need the report today." It is not wrong, but it feels cold. In Britain, we like to open with something warm. Try "Hope you're well" or "Hope you had a good weekend." Just one small line, and the email feels friendly.

Now look at the request. "Send me the numbers" is very strong. We soften it. We write "I was wondering if you could send me the numbers," or "Would it be possible to see the numbers today?" Same request, softer words.

And at the end, don't stop suddenly. Close with "Many thanks" or "Kind regards." Small changes, but the client will feel the difference. The message is the same. It just lands better.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily think about the colleague's English?
options: It is correct, but the tone is too direct
items.why: "The English is correct… But I want to change the tone… It sounds too direct."

items.q: What does Emily say about the first line, "I need the report today"?
options: It is not wrong, but it feels cold
items.why: "It is not wrong, but it feels cold."

items.q: How does Emily want to soften "Send me the numbers"?
options: "I was wondering if you could send me the numbers"
items.why: "We write 'I was wondering if you could send me the numbers.'"

items.q: Why does Emily suggest these small changes?
options: To make the email much longer
Because the client will feel the difference and the message lands better
items.why: Inferência: ela diz que a mensagem é a mesma, mas 'lands better' e o cliente sente a diferença.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's tone with the new colleague?
items.why: Inferência: ela agradece o trabalho e ensina com calma — é gentil, não crítica dura.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "I always open my emails with a warm line." Here, to open an email means to…
items.why: To open an email = abrir/começar o e-mail.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "I will ___ this email with 'Kind regards.'"
items.why: To close = encerrar. Fechamos o e-mail com a despedida.

items.q: "Hope you're well" is used to…
options: start an email in a friendly way
items.why: "Hope you're well" = espero que esteja bem: abertura amistosa.

items.q: "He softened his email, and it landed well with the client." To land well means to…
items.why: To land well = ser bem recebido.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The email was cold. I need to fix the ___."
items.why: Tone = tom. O tom do e-mail estava frio.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em e-mails e reuniões de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the email." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new email style next week." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em uso, implementar.

items.q: "The client pushed back on the cold tone." This means the client…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "I said I would help, and I followed through." This means I…
items.why: Follow through = cumprir, levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Please get back to me by Friday." To get back to someone means to…
items.why: Get back to someone = responder, dar retorno.
